about: The tracking plan (ADR 0036). Every feature asks which signal proves it is used and that it is worth it; every signal is here with the attributes it carries. Edit this file, then run `node tools/tracking-plan.mjs`: it writes docs/telemetry/tracking-plan.md and the frontend's event types. TrackingPlanTests holds the code to it at both ends.

features.name: Search
features.question: What share of typed searches finds nothing, and is it worse for agents than for people?
features.decision: Where the next relevance work goes: synonyms and golden-set queries for the empty ones, or the MCP tool's description if agents come back empty more often than people.

features.name: Browsing by category
features.question: Do people browse the taxonomy, or go straight to search?
features.decision: Whether the category pages earn their place in the navigation.

features.name: Listing filters
features.question: Do shoppers narrow a list, by which facets, on which device, and does a narrowed list lead to a product page more often than the same list unnarrowed?
features.decision: If under 5 % of category visits (category_opened) use a filter in a month, the column opens folded by default. A facet nobody uses in a month is looked at before it is kept, and brand keeps its first place only if it is among the most used. If phones filter far less than desktops, the sheet's batch is the friction to fix next. If narrowed lists do not lead to products more often, the filters are browsing furniture and the next discovery work goes to search instead. Clearing right after an empty result says the counts are misleading.

features.name: Product page
features.question: How do shoppers reach a product — a search, a category, the home page — and how many product views does a cart follow?
features.decision: Where discovery work goes: the search box, the taxonomy or the home page's rows.

features.name: Specs with their source
features.question: Do shoppers open the sentence behind a spec, and do they compare products side by side once they can?
features.decision: If nobody opens a source, the chip is decoration: keep the table, drop the chip's weight and spend review effort elsewhere. If comparisons are made and followed by a cart, the typed half of claims is worth its model and the next source (manuals, datasheets) is worth adding; if they are not, the comparison goes back to being a nice-to-have.

features.name: Cart
features.question: How many carts never become an order, and whose?
features.decision: Whether abandonment work (a saved cart, a reminder) comes before checkout friction.

features.name: Promotions
features.question: What share of orders carries a discount?
features.decision: Whether the promotion engine's combination rules are worth extending, or promotions stay a handful of codes.

features.name: Checkout and payment
features.question: Why does a checkout fail to become an order: a stale screen, a changed price, a declined card, or a provider that did not answer?
features.decision: A stale screen or a price change is our copy and our cache; a decline is the shopper's; an unavailable provider is ours to retry. Each points at a different fix.

features.name: Order page
features.question: Do shoppers come back to follow an order?
features.decision: None today.
features.gap: No decision depends on the answer: the page is the receipt, and it stays whatever the count is. A signal with no decision does not enter the plan.

features.name: Returns
features.question: Why do things come back?
features.decision: Wrong size and not-as-described are the product reasoning layer's case (phase 10); damaged and wrong item are the warehouse's.

features.name: Account and guest cart claim
features.question: Do guests sign in, and does their cart survive it?
features.decision: Whether guest checkout stays the default path.
features.gap: Not measured yet, and not planned: sign-in is the identity provider's, and the claim is one call with no screen of its own. Revisit when accounts do more than hold orders.

features.name: Review queue and publishing
features.question: Does the review queue move: how many drafts become products, and who approves them?
features.decision: Whether publishing needs bulk approval, and later whether the AI proposals of phase 10 are being approved or ignored.

features.name: Withdrawing a product
features.question: How often does a live product have to come back to review, and who pulls it?
features.decision: Whether withdrawing needs a recorded reason, as suspending an agent does, and whether imports should flag the changes that cause it.

features.name: Stock and reservations
features.question: How much held stock never becomes a sale?
features.decision: The hold's lifetime, and whether the expiry sweep the domain has a state for is worth building.

features.name: Catalogue import
features.question: Does an import bring products in?
features.decision: None beyond the run itself.
features.gap: An import is an operator's batch, answered by its own result and its span; a counter would say what the result already says.

features.name: Back-office administration
features.question: Are the orders, returns, promotions, attributes, variants, stock and audit screens used?
features.decision: None at three roles and a handful of users.
features.gap: Every write they make is already an audit row with its actor (ListAuditEntries): that is their evidence, and a metric would count the same thing twice.

features.name: WebMCP
features.question: Do browser agents use the shop's WebMCP tools, which ones, and do they succeed?
features.decision: Which tools to keep, extend or drop; a high share of refusals means a tool's contract is wrong for an agent.

features.name: MCP server and UCP catalogue
features.question: Do external agents call the catalogue over MCP and UCP, which tools, and how often are they refused?
features.decision: Whether the agent checkout of phase 11 has agents waiting for it, and which binding to build it on first.

features.name: AI search layer
features.question: How often is a search answered without one of its AI stages, and how many product changes did the vector layer miss?
features.decision: Whether the AI stages can be on by default, which service to fix first, and when a reindex is due.

features.name: Outbox
features.question: Is eventual consistency still eventual?
features.decision: When a second worker replica, and the row locking it needs, is worth building.

features.name: Claims from descriptions
features.question: How much of what a product's description states reaches the shopkeeper as a claim worth reviewing — and what is refused before they see it?
features.decision: A rising refusal rate for one reason points at one fix: not in the text is the prompt or the model, wrong language is the quantization (P10-0), a failed run is the model server. A queue that keeps failing on a product stops spending the model on it.

features.name: Claim review
features.question: Does the shopkeeper accept what the extractor proposes — and does reviewing the weakest first find the wrong ones?
features.decision: A falling approval rate means the extractor proposes what the shop would not say: revisit the prompt, the model or its settings before the queue stops being read. And of the sure answers a picture gave (sure_answer = true), more than one in ten rejected means the line they clear is too low: raise ProductClaim.SureAnswer before anything is applied without a person.

features.name: Picture doubts
features.question: When the model is sure a picture shows another colour than the catalogue holds, is the picture wrong — or is the model raising what nobody needed raised?
features.decision: Mostly 'the picture is fine' means the line is too low or two colours are one to the shop: raise PictureDoubt.SureDifference, or declare the two as mistaken for each other. A share of 'replace the picture' worth having is what would justify a doubt holding a picture back from being the cover.

features.name: Approved claims reach the catalogue
features.question: Does an approved typed claim become a catalogue attribute, or does Catalog refuse what Knowledge's vetting let through?
features.decision: Any refusal means the vetting and Catalog disagree on the vocabulary — a value vetting accepted that the definition does not: fix the vetting, never loosen the definition. Unchanged at a high rate means the extractor mostly restates attributes the import already set, and the typed half of the prompt is worth less than it costs.

features.name: Test orders
features.question: Do agents rehearse checkouts before they buy for real, and does every rehearsal end — none left holding stock?
features.decision: Rehearsals that are placed but never ended mean the saga stopped short and stock is held for nobody: fix the drain before anything else. Agents that go live without ever rehearsing are the ones whose first failures a customer pays for: make the test credential part of onboarding an agent (P11-3).

features.name: Agent registry
features.question: Do the agents that buy here come from operators the shop knows, or does money arrive through agents nobody registered?
features.decision: A growing share of placed orders from untrusted agents means the registry is not keeping up with who shops here: register the regular ones, and let the agent policy (P11-6) limit what an unknown agent may spend. Nothing from known agents means the registry is not worth its screen yet.

features.name: Shopkeeper dashboard
features.question: Does the shopkeeper start the day on the dashboard, and over which period do they read it?
features.decision: If the dashboard is opened less than the review queue it replaced as the home, the home goes back to the queue. A period nobody chooses is removed; widgets are reordered by what gets read, which is the v2 the task records.
features.gap: Reading is not a write, so there is no audit row, and the question is answered by what is already measured: every widget asks its own endpoint, so http.server.request.duration by route (/api/dashboard/*) and its period query parameter in the span count the openings per figure. A business counter would count the same requests a second time.

features.name: Dashboard tabs and the wall
features.question: Which parts of the shop does the shopkeeper watch — which of the dashboard's tabs are opened — and does anybody put a tab on a monitor of its own?
features.decision: A tab unopened for a month folds into the Overview or goes. If no tab is put on the screen whole in a month, the wall's density and its minute's refresh stay as they are and real time (R-10) is not built for walls.

features.name: Backoffice jobs
features.question: Does the shopkeeper finish their jobs — publish, review a claim, ship, decide a return, suspend an agent, set up a campaign — and how long does each take from opening its screen?
features.decision: A job whose time does not fall after the redesign goes back to R-3; a job that is refused more than it is done points at a screen that invites the wrong action. The before and after are the redesign article's evidence.

features.name: Theme choice
features.question: Does anybody change the theme from the system's, and to which?
features.decision: If nobody changes it within a month of the laboratory's use, the switch goes and the system's preference stays (the redesign's R-3). The storefront's half arrives with R-5.1 as a behavioural event.

features.name: Storefront theme choice
features.question: Do shoppers change the theme from their system's, and does the dark shop hold the same conversion?
features.decision: If nobody changes it in a month, the switch goes and the system's preference stays; if the dark shop converts worse, its product imagery is looked at before anything else.

features.name: Palette and list shortcuts
features.question: Does anybody reach screens and records through the palette, or move down a queue with j and k, and does the pane get used rather than the row?
features.decision: R-6 keeps the shortcuts only if they are used (R-2, P11); a palette nobody opens after a month is simplified to screens alone; a pane nobody acts from goes back to the drawing board in R-3.

features.name: Agent rules
features.question: How often do the shop's own rules for agents refuse an order, which rule, and against agents of what trust?
features.decision: Refusals of known or verified agents by the cap mean the caps are too tight for the agents the shop wants: raise them. Refusals of untrusted agents are the rules working — and a rise in orders_per_hour from one trust level is the signal to look at who is looping. No refusals at all for a month means the rules are not earning their place in checkout's path.

features.name: Added-to-cart notice
features.question: Once a shopper is told a product is in the cart, do they go to the cart from there, or keep shopping?
features.decision: If almost nobody follows it in a month, the notice stays and its link goes: the confirmation is the point, and a link nobody uses is noise beside the one clay action.

features.name: Home page modules
features.question: Which of the home page's modules do shoppers open, and from which place on the page?
features.decision: A module nobody opens in a month moves down or goes; the order of the page follows the numbers.

features.name: Campaign card
features.question: Do shoppers open the campaign card, before a campaign starts as well as while it runs?
features.decision: If the before card is not opened, the teaser is not worth its place.

features.name: Browsing trail
features.question: Do shoppers clear what the shop remembers of their browsing, one entry at a time or all of it?
features.decision: If many clear it, the trail is felt as surveillance; show less, or ask first.

features.name: Suggestions and trends
features.question: Do Puede que te guste and Tendencias lead to products as often as the new arrivals do, and does the vector re-rank beat the rule alone?
features.decision: If suggestions lead to products no more often than the new arrivals do, the rule is not worth its place above them; if the vector re-rank does not beat the rule alone, it is switched off.

features.name: Stock search and filters
features.question: Does the shopkeeper narrow the stock list, by searching or by the restock and sold-out filters, and which?
features.decision: If the search goes unused in a month while the filters are used, restocking is the screen's job and it opens on Restock; if neither is used, the dashboard's figure is where stock is read and the screen keeps only the count.

features.name: Model-call metering
features.question: Are model-call rows being lost before they reach telemetry.ai_invocations?
features.decision: Whether the in-process log needs a larger bound, or a durable queue, before the cost line and the AI usage dashboard can be trusted.

features.name: AI usage and cost
features.question: What do the models cost per day and per model, how fast do they answer, and how often does no model answer Steward?
features.decision: Which profile is Steward's default and which its fallback, and whether a hosted model is worth its price over the local one (S-7).

features.name: Steward
features.question: Is Steward used, from where, what does it cost — and are its proposals worth reviewing, or reviewed at all? Do people start over by choice, and after how many questions?
features.decision: Where it lives and how it is reached; which tools to add or drop; the default profile. Above 30 % rejected, the prompt or the model is the problem, not the screen; unticked at zero batch after batch is the rubber stamp R-2 feared. If the head's new conversation is almost never pressed it leaves the head; if most restarts come from the notice near the window, the window or the history sent is too small.

features.name: Alt text for pictures
features.question: Are the descriptions a model proposes for product pictures good enough to approve as written — and does the job get through its batches, or stall on pictures it cannot read?
features.decision: Below half approved unedited, the job stops proposing in batches and proposes on request, one picture at a time. Failed or skipped above one in five is the model or the store, not the reviewer: the prompt, the profile or the pictures are what changes.

features.name: Pictures read for claims
features.question: Does the job that has product pictures read get through its batches, or stall on pictures it cannot read or a model that does not answer in the shape asked for?
features.decision: Failed or skipped above one in five is the model or the store, not the catalogue: the instructions, the profile or the pictures are what changes before any claim is proposed from a reading. Whether the claims read from pictures are worth reviewing is measured where they are decided, with the review queue's own events.

features.name: Tino
features.question: Is Tino used, and from where; what kind of answer does it give and how much of what the model writes survives; does an answer lead to a product — and when it does not answer, why? Do shoppers start over, and after how many questions?
features.decision: Where its door lives and whether the search page's offer earns its place; above 20 % of sentences dropped, the prompt or the model is the problem; if answers lead to products no more than search results do, the conversation is not worth its cost; the turn's seconds, the shop's daily budget and the default profile. If the cards code adds under *Matches your search* are opened far less than those the model explained, topping an answer up to three stops. If shoppers start over after one or two questions, the history drags answers off topic and what a turn sends of it is what changes; if nobody ever does, the head's button goes.

features.name: Search with a picture
features.question: Does anyone search with a picture, from where, do they mark a part, how much of what they photograph does the shop sell, and does the picture find what they wanted?
features.decision: If almost nobody does, the control leaves the search box for the search page; if results are followed no more often than the words' are, text against pictures is not worth making a leg of the main search; if most searches are refused or fail, the limits or the model's place are wrong. If most are marked, the detector matters less than the box and its cost is questioned; many objects not sold is the catalogue's gap, measured; and whether Tino gets pictures (the camera search's stage 2) is decided on these.

features.name: Speak to the shop
features.question: Does anyone speak to the shop, does it understand them, and are the words it hears good enough to send?
features.decision: If almost nobody speaks after a month of traffic, the microphone leaves the search box and stays in Tino only; if one adapter's words are edited or discarded far more often than the other's, the default moves; if most questions are not heard, the engine or its model is wrong for this shop.

features.name: Kits
features.question: Are kits asked for, and can the shop fill them at the budgets people give; is a solved kit worth buying; and does a sentence get a shopper to a kit?
features.decision: A template mostly left with empty required slots at common budgets needs cheaper candidates in the catalogue, or to go; built often and added seldom means the choices are not trusted, and the explanation is what to work on before anything else. Most sentences naming no kit means the box asks the wrong thing or the shop lacks the kits people want: reword it, add those kits, or take the box out; understood sentences seldom built into a kit means what was read is not what was meant.

features.name: The shopper's account
features.question: Do returning shoppers use what the account remembers at checkout, is checkout where the address book gets filled, do saved cards go stale, and is erasure used?
features.decision: If almost every signed-in order still types its address, the book is not reachable enough at checkout, and checkout changes before the account grows another section; if checkout fills the book, the account's own form stays plain; a high share of saved cards declined means the wallet warns before expiry, not at the till. Erasure changes nothing in the product: it is the evidence the operation is real, and the number the article quotes.

features.name: Importing a store
features.question: Is the Shopify source used, and how much of a store comes across clean, per context?
features.decision: A high count of CategoryNotMapped moves collections or a proposed taxonomy mapping up the plan; DescriptionHadLayout decides whether descriptions keep their tables (docs/specs/shopify-import.md). For stock, LocationNotMapped and VariantNotInCatalogue say whether the locations file and the order of imports need a tool of their own. Gift cards listed for reissue, counted per store, say whether Tendero needs gift cards of its own (docs/specs/shopify-leave.md, decision 6). A rehearsal of the whole migration never followed by one for real says the answer stopped the merchant, and its notes say which step to work on first.

features.name: Exports and feeds
features.question: Which exports are used, and in which format: is the product feed fetched, is the catalogue taken to another platform, do orders go to an accountant?
features.decision: Orders exported often in CSV decide whether XLSX earns its dependency (docs/specs/exports.md, decision 3); a feed fetched every day decides whether a Merchant API client is worth building over a fetched file. The rows each feed carries, against the products on sale, say whether the feed loses any on the way.

features.name: Sales channels
features.question: Does a sales channel keep up with the catalogue, how often does it refuse what it is told, and do its orders arrive — by which path?
features.decision: A refusal rate above a few in a hundred means the mapping loses data, fixed before a second channel is added; failures that pile up mean the reconciliation, not the outbox, is carrying the channel (docs/specs/shopify-channel.md, Evidence of use). Orders found only by the reconciliation mean the webhooks are failing — the subscription or the URL, not the code. Any oversold order raises the stock margin (2 units today) or shortens the reconciliation. Any order held longer than a day is a mapping to fix, not a list to watch, and an order held because its figures do not add up is a bug (P16-29).

features.name: A store's old addresses
features.question: After a shop leaves its store, are the store's old addresses still visited, and do they still lead somewhere?
features.decision: When redirected requests fall to nothing the table of collections can go; a high share of missing ones says which handles or collections the import did not keep (docs/specs/shopify-leave.md, decision 7).

events.name: webmcp_tool_invoked
events.description: A browser agent called one of the shop's WebMCP tools. Emitted with actor `webmcp`.

tool.description: The tool's registered name; never its arguments.

outcome.description: Refused is the shop saying no; failed is the tool breaking.

events.name: product_viewed
events.description: A shopper opened a product page. Only with analytics consent.

arrived_from.description: The page before this one, by kind; listing is a list made only of filters (Ofertas, Novedades), direct when there was none in this tab. From the home page, the row that led here when it says so: trail (Sigue donde lo dejaste), campaign (the campaign card), suggested (Puede que te guste) and trending (Tendencias) — R-8.

filtered.description: Whether the list the shopper came from was narrowed by filters. False for a page that is not a list.

events.name: category_opened
events.description: A shopper opened a category listing (R-0 of the redesign). Only with analytics consent.

arrived_from.description: How the shopper got there: menu once the storefront has one (R-5), otherwise the kind of page before this one; direct when there was none in this tab. The kind and never the URL.

events.name: filter_applied
events.description: A shopper narrowed a list by a facet, or changed a facet's choices (R-7.3, F-6): once per facet a choice changed, when it takes effect — at once in the column, with Ver N productos in the phone's sheet. Only with analytics consent. A browser agent's apply_filter is counted by webmcp_tool_invoked, not here.

facet.description: The facet's code: category, brand, price, offer, new or stock, or an attribute's catalogue code (COLOR, SIZE). Never the value chosen.

listing.description: The kind of list narrowed: a category page, a search's results, or a list made only of filters (Ofertas, Novedades).

surface.description: The desktop's column, which applies each choice, or the phone's sheet, which applies a batch.

events.name: filters_cleared
events.description: A shopper took every filter off a list at once (R-7.3, F-6). Only with analytics consent.

surface.description: Quitar todo beside the chips, the one offered by a list that filters emptied, or the phone's sheet.

events.name: spec_source_opened
events.description: A shopper opened the words behind a spec — the quote and its support. Only with analytics consent.

source.description: Where the value came from; only a value an approved claim put there has words to open.

events.name: products_compared
events.description: A shopper opened a side-by-side comparison. Only with analytics consent.

products.description: How many products were compared, two to four.

events.name: backoffice_view_opened
events.description: The shopkeeper opened a backoffice screen (R-0 of the redesign). A staff event: sent by default under the shop's notice to staff, and never with who they are.

view.description: The screen, by its route; never an id in it. The dashboard's Overview is dashboard, each of its tabs dashboard.<tab> (R-9).

events.name: backoffice_action_taken
events.description: The shopkeeper did what a screen is for — published, approved, shipped, decided, suspended — and how the server answered (R-0). A staff event.

view.description: The screen it was done on.

action.description: What was done, from a closed list.

outcome.description: done; refused when the server said no (a 4xx, a rule); failed when it could not answer.

via.description: Where it was pressed: on the list's row, in the pane beside it, or as the page's own action (R-3's adoption signal for the pane).

events.name: backoffice_theme_chosen
events.description: A staff member chose light, dark or the system's theme in the account menu (the redesign's R-3). A staff event under the shop's notice (ADR 0041), never with who they are.

theme.description: What was chosen, not what the system resolved it to.

events.name: backoffice_affordance_used
events.description: A staff member reached something through the command palette or a list shortcut rather than by pointing (the redesign's R-4.6), or narrowed a list by searching or filtering it (R-7.1). A staff event under the shop's notice (ADR 0041), never with who they are.

affordance.description: The palette (Ctrl K or /), j and k down a queue, a list's search box and filter chips (R-7.1), or a dashboard tab put on the screen whole (R-9).

target.description: What it reached; never which one.

events.name: theme_chosen
events.description: A shopper chose light, dark or the system's theme (the redesign's R-5.1). Behavioural, so it waits for analytics consent.

theme.description: What was chosen, not what the system resolved it to.

events.name: cart_notice_followed
events.description: A shopper followed the link in the notice that says a product went into the cart (the redesign's R-5.3, raised by the baseline walkthrough). Behavioural, so it waits for analytics consent.

events.name: home_module_opened
events.description: A shopper followed a link inside one of the home page's modules (R-8). Only with analytics consent.

module.description: Which module: the campaign card, Sigue donde lo dejaste, Compra con tu agente, Ofertas, Puede que te guste, Tendencias, Lo más vendido, Novedades or Secciones de la tienda.

position.description: Where the module was on the page when it was opened, from 1 at the top, counting only the modules drawn — a band that failed or had nothing to show does not take a place.

events.name: campaign_card_opened
events.description: A shopper followed the campaign card's call to action or one of its products (R-8). Only with analytics consent.

campaign.description: The campaign's code (TENDERO_DAYS): a handful per year, set by the shopkeeper, never a person or a product.

phase.description: Before the campaign starts (Empieza en…) or while it runs (Termina en…).

events.name: trail_cleared
events.description: A shopper removed their browsing trail, one entry or all of it (R-8). Only with analytics consent.

scope.description: One product or one search removed, or the whole trail.

events.name: steward_opened
events.description: The shopkeeper opened Steward's panel, from the bar or the palette (phase 12). A staff event: never who, never what they ask.

view.description: The screen it was opened on.

events.name: steward_answered
events.description: A Steward turn came back. Never the question's text nor the answer's: what it read, what it cost, which profile answered.

status.description: StewardStatus, as the turn answered it.

tools.description: How many reads the turn made.

calls.description: Model calls the turn took, six at most.

cost.description: What the turn cost, in micro-euros; 0 on a local profile.

profile.description: The profile that answered, as configured (local, a hosted one's name): a handful, set by the shop. none when no profile answered; which one failed is the metric tendero.ai.calls, by profile and outcome.

fell_back.description: Whether a profile after the first answered.

events.name: proposals_reviewed
events.description: A batch a model proposed was decided through the review: Steward's proposals, or a product's claims together. Sent once the server answered, counting what it did to each row; the counts, never what they said.

kind.description: Steward's proposals, or a product's claims (S-5).

proposed.description: How many the review showed waiting, counted by the batch's first decision: a reject after an approve of the same batch sends 0.

approved.description: How many this decision approved, as the server answered: a stale or failed row is not one.

unticked.description: How many the person unticked, counted by the batch's first decision like proposed: a rubber stamp leaves this at zero, batch after batch.

events.name: steward_unavailable
events.description: A Steward turn found no model to answer it: the default failed, and the fallback too when there is one.

fell_back.description: Whether a fallback profile was tried as well.

events.name: steward_conversation_restarted
events.description: The shopkeeper started a new conversation with Steward, forgetting the one on screen: from the panel's head when they chose to, or from the notice near the model's window or the end of a conversation when Steward asked. Never what was said.

from.description: The head's button, the notice near the model's window, or the button that replaces the composer once the conversation is over.

exchanges.description: How many questions the conversation forgotten had.

events.name: tino_opened
events.description: A shopper opened Tino's panel, from the header or from the search page's offer (phase 12b). Only with analytics consent; never what they ask.

from.description: The header's door, or the search page's *Ask Tino this*.

page.description: The kind of page it was opened on.

events.name: tino_answered
events.description: Tino answered a turn (phase 12b). The kind of answer and its counts, never the question nor a sentence of the answer. Only with analytics consent.

reasons.description: Sentences the shopper is shown, each with the fact it cites.

reasons_dropped.description: Sentences the model wrote that did not hold and were not shown.

events.name: tino_result_followed
events.description: A shopper followed something an answer of Tino's offered (phase 12b): a product, the order's page, or all the search's results. Only with analytics consent.

position.description: For a product, its place in the answer, from 1; 0 otherwise.

card.description: For a product, whether its card carried the model's reasons or only code's line that the search found it (2026-10-21); none for anything else.

events.name: tino_unavailable
events.description: Tino did not answer and the panel showed the search results instead, or said it is not available (phase 12b). Only with analytics consent.

cause.description: The turn's cause; too_many for the rate limit, network when the request itself failed, not_available when the door was opened while Tino is off.

events.name: tino_conversation_restarted
events.description: A shopper started a new conversation with Tino from the panel's head, forgetting the one on screen. Only with analytics consent; never what was said.

exchanges.description: How many questions the conversation forgotten had.

events.name: image_alt_proposal_decided
events.description: A proposed alt text for a product picture was decided by a person: approved as the model wrote it, approved after the person corrected it, or rejected. The decision and the language of the screen, never the words.

decision.description: What the person did with the proposal.

events.name: search_by_image_submitted
events.description: A shopper gave the shop a picture to search with (phase 13a). Only with analytics consent; never the picture, its name or anything read from it.

how.description: How the picture was given: chosen, dropped or pasted from the device, taken with the phone's own camera app, or with the shop's viewfinder in the page (the camera search, CS-6).

outcome.description: What the shop did with it: an answer, a refusal of the file, the minute's limit, or not answering.

results.description: How many products came back, every block's together; 0 when none did or it was not answered.

marked.description: The shopper marked a part, so only that part was sent (the camera search, CS-1.2). Mostly marked means the detector matters less than the box.

objects.description: How many objects were found in what was sent, sold or not; 1 when the shop could not look for objects and searched it whole.

not_sold.description: How many of those are of a kind the shop does not sell: the catalogue's gap, counted. Never which kinds.

words.description: Words were added to narrow the blocks (CS-4). Never the words.

events.name: search_by_image_result_followed
events.description: A shopper opened a product from the answer to a picture (phase 13a). Only with analytics consent.

position.description: Its place in the answer, from 1.

block.description: The object's number in the picture whose block it was opened from, from 1 (the camera search, CS-3); 0 from a list of its own. Whether a picture leads to a product from the first block only.

events.name: voice_input_heard
events.description: A shopper spoke a question and listening ended (phase 14). Only with analytics consent; never the audio or the words.

where.description: Which box: Tino's composer, the phone's search box, or Steward's composer in the backoffice.

adapter.description: Which adapter listened: the shop's own engine, or the browser's on the device.

outcome.description: What listening came to: words for the box, nothing heard, a failure, or Escape.

events.name: voice_transcript_used
events.description: What became of the words a microphone wrote into a box (phase 14). Only with analytics consent; never the words.

where.description: Which box: Tino's composer, the phone's search box, or Steward's composer in the backoffice.

adapter.description: Which adapter listened: the shop's own engine, or the browser's on the device.

how.description: Sent as they were heard, sent after the shopper changed them, or never sent.

events.name: kit_built
events.description: A shopper asked the shop to build a kit and got an answer (phase 13c, K-5): once per kit built, complete or not. Only with analytics consent.

template.description: The kit's code, as the shop's file names it (KITCHEN_STARTER). A closed set: the templates the shop wrote.

budget.description: The budget asked for, as a band in the shop's currency. Never the figure typed.

filled.description: How many slots got a product.

empty.description: How many slots were left empty, required or not.

binding.description: What held the kit back: nothing, the budget, or the shop having nothing for a slot.

source.description: Whether the request came from the form or from a sentence a model read into it (K-6).

events.name: kit_added_to_cart
events.description: A shopper put a built kit in the cart (phase 13c, K-5): once per kit added, with every line it could add. Only with analytics consent.

template.description: The kit's code, as in kit_built.

lines.description: How many products were added: one a filled slot.

events.name: kit_sentence_read
events.description: A shopper wrote what kit they want and the shop read it (phase 13c, K-6): once per sentence sent, understood or not. Never the sentence itself. Only with analytics consent.

understood.description: Whether the sentence named one of the shop's kits. Not understood, the shopper is left with the list.

template.description: The kit it named, as in kit_built; none when it named none.

budget.description: Whether the sentence said a budget, read by code.

events.name: checkout_prefilled
events.description: A signed-in shopper placed an order (P15-3, P15-5): whether the address and the way to pay came from the account or were typed now. Only with analytics consent; never the address or the card.

address.description: Sent to an entry of the address book, or to an address typed at checkout.

method.description: Paid with a card kept in the wallet, or a new one.

events.name: address_kept_at_checkout
events.description: A new address typed at checkout was kept in the address book by its box (P15-3). Only with analytics consent; never the address or its label.

kept.description: Whether it was kept; false when the order was placed and keeping it failed.

events.name: saved_method_declined
events.description: A card kept in the wallet was declined at checkout (P15-5). Only with analytics consent; never the card.

expired.description: Whether the wallet already said the card had expired; checkout never offers one, so true means a card that expired between the page and the till.

metrics.name: tendero.search.degraded
metrics.description: Searches answered without one of their AI stages, by stage.

stage.description: The stage that did not answer.

metrics.name: tendero.search.vector_projection.failed
metrics.description: Product changes the vector layer could not take; the lexical index took them.

metrics.name: tendero.search.picture_projection.failed
metrics.description: Product changes the picture vectors could not take; the lexical index took them.

metrics.name: tendero.outbox.lag
metrics.description: Seconds between an event being raised and processed.

metrics.name: tendero.search.requests
metrics.description: Searches answered, by who asked, through what, typed or browsed, and whether anything came back.

actor.kind.description: Agent for MCP and UCP, and for a principal carrying an agent id; human otherwise (ADR 0036).

surface.description: The route the request came through. WebMCP inherits the shopper's session, so to the server it is the web; its evidence is `webmcp_tool_invoked`.

mode.description: Query when text was typed; browse when it was not — a category page, a home-page row.

category.description: Whether the search was narrowed to a category.

result.description: Whether the first page had any product.

metrics.name: tendero.carts.created
metrics.description: Carts opened. Against placed orders, it is abandonment: nothing sets a cart to Abandoned yet, so the difference is the measure.

actor.kind.description: Agent for MCP and UCP, and for a principal carrying an agent id; human otherwise (ADR 0036).

surface.description: The route the request came through. WebMCP inherits the shopper's session, so to the server it is the web; its evidence is `webmcp_tool_invoked`.

metrics.name: tendero.checkout.attempts
metrics.description: Every place-order attempt by its outcome; orders placed are the ones whose outcome is placed.

actor.kind.description: Agent for MCP and UCP, and for a principal carrying an agent id; human otherwise (ADR 0036).

surface.description: The route the request came through. WebMCP inherits the shopper's session, so to the server it is the web; its evidence is `webmcp_tool_invoked`.

order.mode.description: Test when the credential that placed it is a test one (ADR 0038): the Shop pulse leaves it out, and a rehearsal is read on its own.

agent.trust.description: How far the shop trusts the agent behind the attempt (P11-2): none for a person, untrusted for an agent nobody registered.

outcome.description: PlaceOrderOutcome, labelled by MetricLabels. not_mandated (P11-5): an agent's total outside what its verified mandate approved — how often agents try to spend what the person did not approve. insufficient_stock (phase 13b): the cart asked for more than the shelf had, refused at the till before any money — a share that grows says the basket's own note is not being read, or stock is being shown that is not there.

discounted.description: Whether any promotion applied to the order.

metrics.name: tendero.agents.denials
metrics.description: Agent orders the shop's own rules refused (P11-6), by rule and by how far the shop trusts the agent.

rule.description: The first rule in the table that denied.

agent.trust.description: The agent's standing in the registry; untrusted for one nobody registered.

metrics.name: tendero.orders.test_ended
metrics.description: Test orders that went all the way to confirmed and ended there, their stock given back.

metrics.name: tendero.returns.requested
metrics.description: Lines of the returns opened, by their reason: the closed set of five a buyer chooses from, kept by the domain for exactly this analysis.

reason.description: ReturnReason, labelled by MetricLabels. unstated is never counted: it is the reason of a refund an import brought (ADR 0066), which no buyer opened, and opening a return refuses it.

metrics.name: tendero.catalog.products.published
metrics.description: Products moved from Draft to Active.

actor.kind.description: Agent for MCP and UCP, and for a principal carrying an agent id; human otherwise (ADR 0036).

metrics.name: tendero.catalog.import.products
metrics.description: Products an import created, updated or failed, by source.

catalog.source.description: The source imported from: seed, shopify (phase 16).

catalog.import.outcome.description: What happened to the product, counted once its batch is saved.

metrics.name: tendero.catalog.import.notes
metrics.description: What a source did not hand over cleanly, by source and code.

metrics.name: tendero.catalog.source_addresses
metrics.description: A store's old addresses asked for, by kind and whether they led somewhere.

catalog.address.kind.description: What the old address named: /products/<handle>, or /collections/<handle>.

catalog.address.outcome.description: Answered with a 301 to a page on sale, or with a 404.

metrics.name: tendero.inventory.import.levels
metrics.description: Stock levels an import counted or skipped, by source.

catalog.source.description: The source imported from; the same label as the catalogue import, so one query reads a store across contexts.

inventory.import.outcome.description: Counted into a warehouse the shop operates, or skipped because the shop does not operate it.

metrics.name: tendero.inventory.import.notes
metrics.description: What a stock source did not hand over cleanly, by source and code.

metrics.name: tendero.accounts.import.customers
metrics.description: Customers an import created, found already imported or linked, by source.

catalog.source.description: The source imported from; the same label as the catalogue and stock imports.

accounts.import.outcome.description: Made here, brought by an earlier import, or a person the shop already had, linked through their identity.

metrics.name: tendero.accounts.import.notes
metrics.description: What a customer source did not hand over cleanly, by source and code.

metrics.name: tendero.ordering.import.orders
metrics.description: Orders an import created or found already imported, and refunds it brought, by source.

catalog.source.description: The source imported from; the same label as the catalogue, stock and customer imports.

ordering.import.outcome.description: An order made here, one an earlier import brought, or a refund brought as a return born refunded.

metrics.name: tendero.ordering.import.notes
metrics.description: What an order source did not hand over cleanly, by source and code.

metrics.name: tendero.ordering.import.gift_cards
metrics.description: Gift cards an import listed for the merchant to reissue, by source.

metrics.name: tendero.exports.generated
metrics.description: Exports and feeds written, by kind and format.

export.kind.description: What left the shop: the product feed, the catalogue for another platform, orders for the accountant.

export.format.description: The format it was written in: google-merchant, shopify-csv, csv.

metrics.name: tendero.exports.rows
metrics.description: The rows an export or a feed carried, by kind and format.

export.format.description: The format it was written in.

metrics.name: tendero.channel.publications
metrics.description: Every product, stock or shipment publication to a sales channel, by its outcome.

kind.description: What was published: a product, a SKU's available quantity, or that an order the channel took was shipped.

outcome.description: Published; stale (the channel sold since, kept its number, and the sale's order will move Tendero's); refused by the channel; nothing to tell (archived before it was ever published); or failed, left to the reconciliation.

metrics.name: tendero.channel.orders.received
metrics.description: Every order a sales channel took that Tendero read, by the path it came by and what became of it.

channel.description: The channel that took it: shopify.

path.description: How Tendero heard of it: the channel's webhook, the reconciliation's pass, or read again by its id while held (P16-29).

outcome.description: Received to be shipped; already received by the other path; or skipped, and why.

metrics.name: tendero.channel.orders.held
metrics.description: Every order a sales channel took that Tendero could not receive and holds to read again, by why (P16-29).

channel.description: The channel that took it: shopify.

reason.description: Why it could not be received: each a reason that can be mended.

metrics.name: tendero.channel.orders.released
metrics.description: Every held order that left the list: received at last, or closed on the channel (P16-29).

channel.description: The channel that took it: shopify.

outcome.description: Received at last, or cancelled, fulfilled or gone on the channel.

metrics.name: tendero.channel.oversold
metrics.description: Orders a sales channel took for stock that could not be held: the evidence the stock margin is judged by.

channel.description: The channel that took it: shopify.

metrics.name: tendero.migration.runs
metrics.description: A store's migrations run as one operation, rehearsed or for real, by source.

migration.rehearsal.description: Whether the run was a rehearsal, which wrote nothing.

metrics.name: tendero.pricing.import.discounts
metrics.description: Discounts a proposal turned into promotions or left out, by source.

catalog.source.description: The source imported from; the same label as the other imports.

pricing.import.outcome.description: Written to the proposal of promotions, or left out with a note saying why.

metrics.name: tendero.pricing.import.notes
metrics.description: What a discount source could not hand over as the store ran it, by source and code.

metrics.name: tendero.catalog.products.withdrawn
metrics.description: Products moved from Active back to Draft.

actor.kind.description: Agent for MCP and UCP, and for a principal carrying an agent id; human otherwise (ADR 0036).

metrics.name: tendero.inventory.reservations
metrics.description: Reservation transitions, by the state they reach.

status.description: ReservationStatus, labelled by MetricLabels. Expired is never recorded yet: nothing expires a hold.

metrics.name: tendero.agent.tool_calls
metrics.description: Calls from external agents to the MCP tools and the UCP catalogue operations.

surface.description: The binding the call came through.

tool.description: The tool or operation name; a closed set of the ones served.

outcome.description: Refused is the shop saying no; failed is the tool breaking.

refusal.description: The refusal's code when the shop said no with one (Invalid, ProductNotFound, TooFewToCompare): a closed set, the codes the tools declare. Absent when the call was answered or broke. A code that dominates is a tool whose description or contract is wrong for an agent.

metrics.name: tendero.knowledge.claims.proposed
metrics.description: Claims proposed for review, by the extractor that read the text.

extractor.description: Which extractor read the source: the rules or the model for a description, and for a picture's reading the code that reads back what the picture answered.

metrics.name: tendero.knowledge.claims.dropped
metrics.description: Claims an extractor proposed that code refused before any person saw them, by reason.

metrics.name: tendero.knowledge.proposals.failed
metrics.description: Proposal runs that failed on a product; retried until its limit.

metrics.name: tendero.knowledge.descriptions.failed
metrics.description: Product changes whose description Knowledge could not record; the next save records it.

metrics.name: tendero.knowledge.claims.reviewed
metrics.description: Claims a person approved or rejected, by decision.

sure_answer.description: Whether the claim was a picture's own answer the model was sure of (at or above ProductClaim.SureAnswer): the ones a person may approve in bulk.

metrics.name: tendero.knowledge.picture_doubts.decided
metrics.description: Doubts about a picture a person decided, by what they said of it.

metrics.name: tendero.knowledge.picture_doubts.retagged
metrics.description: Pictures Catalog was asked to file under another variant after a doubt was decided, by what it answered.

outcome.description: ImageShowsOutcome, labelled by MetricLabels: 'not_sold' is a person saying a picture is of a colour no variant is sold in.

metrics.name: tendero.knowledge.claims.applied
metrics.description: Approved typed claims Catalog was asked to hold, by what it answered.

metrics.name: tendero.ai.invocations.dropped
metrics.description: Model-call rows dropped because the log was full.

metrics.name: tendero.ai.calls
metrics.description: Model calls, by operation, profile, model and outcome. Never by conversation: the rows carry that.

operation.description: What the call was for: steward.turn, knowledge.extract.

profile.description: The profile that was called, by its configuration name.

metrics.name: tendero.ai.cost
metrics.description: What model calls cost at their profile's price at that moment, in micro-euros.

operation.description: What the call was for: steward.turn, knowledge.extract.

profile.description: The profile that was called, by its configuration name.

metrics.name: tendero.steward.turns
metrics.description: Steward's turns, by how they ended and whether a fallback profile was reached.

fell_back.description: Whether a profile after the first was reached.

metrics.name: tendero.tino.turns
metrics.description: Tino's turns, by status, by cause when it did not answer, and by the kind of answer.

cause.description: TinoCause, labelled by MetricLabels; none when Tino answered.

kind.description: TinoKind, labelled by MetricLabels; none when Tino did not answer.

metrics.name: tendero.alt_text.pictures
metrics.description: Pictures the alt-text job took, by what became of each.

outcome.description: proposed: a description was stored for a person to review. skipped: the store had no such picture, or its bytes were not one. failed: the model did not describe it in a way that can be proposed.

metrics.name: tendero.picture_reading.pictures
metrics.description: Pictures the reading job took, by what became of each.

outcome.description: read: the model's description was kept as a document, in both languages. skipped: the store had no such picture, or its bytes were not one. failed: the model did not describe it in a way that can be kept.

metrics.name: tendero.accounts.erased
metrics.description: Accounts removed by their owner (P15-9): a count, with no identity, and nothing else about them.
